findings.title: Commit markers are checkbox items in standalone "Commit" tasks
findings.description: Tasks 1.5, 2.4, 3.6, 4.3 and 5.5 are separate tasks that only commit, and each one writes the marker as a checklist item (`- [ ] **Commit:** ...`). Commit markers must be plain lines, never checkboxes. Remove the five "Commit" tasks. Put a plain `**Commit**: <message>` line after the last task in each section (1.4, 2.3, 3.5, 4.2, 5.4), and drop the `git add` sub-items. The section ends are the right places to commit; only the format is wrong.

findings.title: Section 4 commits changed shipped configs without running tests
findings.description:
Tasks 4.1 and 4.2 switch `config/default.yaml` and `config/test.yaml` to `policy: wrap` and only check that they load with a one-line `python -c`. Task 4.3 then commits. At least two tests read the real shipped config:
- `tests/test_config.py:45` loads `config/default.yaml`.
- `tests/test_main.py:70` starts the server with it.

So the commit is not a tested point. The full test run only happens later, in Task 5.1. Add a `pytest tests/test_config.py tests/test_main.py` step (or a full `pytest`) to Section 4 before its commit marker. Then Task 5.1 duplicates Task 5.2 step 2 and can be dropped.

findings.title: Task 1.1 adds an import that already exists
findings.description: `from enum import StrEnum` is already imported at line 7, and `_serialize_for_yaml` uses it. Task 1.1's step "Add `from enum import StrEnum` to imports" should say "confirm it is imported" instead. Otherwise a junior agent may add a duplicate import.

findings.title: Round-trip criterion (SC5) holds against the current code
findings.description: `config_to_yaml` already passes the data through `_serialize_for_yaml`, which turns `StrEnum` values into plain strings before `yaml.dump`. The round-trip test in Task 1.4 should therefore pass without changing the serializer. SC5 also asks that reloading gives an equal `ServerConfig`, and Task 1.4 only asserts the policy field. Comparing the whole object (`assert reloaded == original`) would match the criterion exactly at no extra cost. This is minor.

findings.title: Wrap with float `np.mod` can land exactly on `width`
findings.description: For very small negative values, float `np.mod(-1e-17, 100.0)` returns `100.0`. That breaks the half-open `[0, width)` rule in SC7, and it could make the strict `x < width` check in Task 3.4's `test_wrap_policy_keeps_all_positions_inside` fail now and then. Optionally, add to Task 2.2 a step that maps any result equal to `width`/`height` back to 0, plus one unit test for it. No success criterion is unmet with today's test inputs, so this is a note.

findings.title: Unit test list is slightly heavier than needed
findings.description:
Task 2.3 lists about 19 tests for an effort-2/5 slice. Three can be merged or cut:
- `test_open_is_noop_positions` and `test_open_is_noop_velocities` can be one test.
- The parametrized "dispatches and does not raise" test adds nothing over the per-policy tests.
- `test_reflect_policy_flips_velocities_at_edges` in Task 3.4 repeats `test_reflect_clamps_right_edge`.

The rest maps directly to SC6–SC9.

findings.title: Sequencing and test-with pattern
findings.description: Every implementation task is followed straight away by its tests (1.4, 2.3, 3.4). There are no circular dependencies. The constructor change that breaks other tests (3.1) is fixed before Section 3 commits (3.4/3.5).

findings.title: No load test task
findings.description: The slice states no NFR. "Zero overhead" for `OPEN` is a design property, and Task 3.4's mock test checks it. This project's `.claude/rules/python.md` has no load-test-tier rule, so I am not asking for a `tests/load/` task. Another `python.md` outside this project, two folders up under `squadron/.claude/rules/`, does require load tests on simulation paths; it would apply only if this project adopts that rule set.

findings.title: Frontmatter says complete while every box is unchecked
findings.description: `status: complete` disagrees with the checklist, where no box is ticked. Set it to `not-started` (or whatever status the project uses before implementation) until Task 5.3 sets it.
